top_stories.title: OpenAI Floats Giving Trump Administration 5 Percent Cut of AI Boom
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has proposed offering the Trump administration a 5 percent stake in its commercial upside as part of ongoing negotiations over its relationship with the US government. The move signals OpenAI's efforts to align itself with the current administration amid broader debates over AI governance and regulation.

top_stories.title: Agentic AI Puts $234B in Enterprise SaaS Spending at Risk, Gartner Says
top_stories.summary: Gartner warns that the rise of agentic AI could put $234 billion in enterprise SaaS spending at risk as AI agents increasingly automate tasks previously handled by traditional software applications. The forecast underscores the potentially disruptive impact of autonomous AI systems on established software business models.

top_stories.title: Microsoft Frontier Company: AI Engineering That Amplifies and Protects Your Intelligence
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has published a blog post outlining its 'Frontier Company' vision, describing how it is embedding AI engineering across its products to amplify human capability while building in safeguards. The post covers AI infrastructure investments and Microsoft's broader strategy for integrating AI into enterprise and consumer offerings.

top_stories.title: Can Cursor Remain a Platform for OpenAI and Anthropic's Models Inside SpaceX?
top_stories.summary: Wired reports on the question of whether Cursor, the AI coding tool, can maintain its open, multi-model platform approach after being adopted inside SpaceX, where access to certain AI providers may be restricted. The story explores the tensions between enterprise security requirements and the flexibility that makes AI coding tools attractive to developers.

top_stories.title: The Download: Anthropic Launches Claude Science, and California's Carbon Manure Math
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports on Anthropic's launch of Claude Science, a specialised AI capability aimed at scientific research and discovery. The newsletter also covers a separate story on the environmental accounting around California's carbon offset schemes.

further_links.title: The Download: A Startup Has a Solution for AI's Groupthink Problem
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review covers a startup working to address the tendency of large language models to converge on similar outputs, a phenomenon described as AI groupthink.

further_links.title: Now We're Getting AI Fake News Complaining About How AI Fake News Is the Death of Real News
further_links.summary: Nieman Lab examines the emergence of AI-generated content that itself decries the harms of AI misinformation, highlighting a new layer of complexity in the AI and media integrity debate.

further_links.title: Weird Al Yankovic Pulled Out of AI Ad Deal: 'I Can't Be the Poster Boy for AI'
further_links.summary: Weird Al Yankovic has revealed he turned down a significant financial offer to appear in an AI advertisement, citing ethical concerns about being publicly associated with the technology.

further_links.title: The Gauge Broke: Devs Felt 20% Faster With AI, Measured 19% Slower (2025)
further_links.summary: A blog post examines research finding that developers using AI coding tools reported feeling significantly more productive, but objective measurements showed they were actually slower, raising questions about how AI productivity gains are perceived versus realised.

further_links.title: Forbes 2026 AI 50 List: Top Artificial Intelligence Companies
further_links.summary: Forbes has published its annual list of the 50 most promising private AI companies, offering a snapshot of the current AI industry landscape.

further_links.title: Achieving Operational Excellence With AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review looks at how organisations are deploying AI to improve operational efficiency, with case studies and analysis of best practices for enterprise AI adoption.

further_links.title: Meta Is Charging a Subscription for Smart Glasses Features. Welcome to the New Era of Consumer Tech [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports that Meta is introducing a subscription tier for advanced features on its AI-powered smart glasses, reflecting a broader shift in how consumer AI hardware is being monetised.

further_links.title: AI Can't Be Listed as Inventor on Patent Applications, Japan's Top Court Rules
further_links.summary: Japan's supreme court has ruled that AI systems cannot be named as inventors on patent applications, aligning the country with similar decisions in other major jurisdictions.

further_links.title: Euromonitor Updates Passport Intelligence Platform With AI Features
further_links.summary: Euromonitor International has added AI-powered capabilities to its Passport market intelligence platform, aiming to help businesses extract faster insights from its global data.

further_links.title: Seekr and Enabled Intelligence Partner to Deliver Explainable AI for Enterprise Applications
further_links.summary: Seekr and Enabled Intelligence have announced a partnership to bring explainable AI tools to enterprise clients, targeting transparency and accountability in AI-driven decision-making.
